guide.summary: Todoist API v1 supports OAuth2 user authorization for individual accounts, and the documented data:read scope covers read-only access to tasks. Setup requires app registration and token exchange, and distribution to other customer workspaces is not established by the supplied sources.

findings.title: OAuth2 user authorization for connected Todoist accounts
findings.detail: External applications obtain a user-authorized API token through OAuth2. The flow uses the authorization endpoint with client_id, scope and response_type=code, then exchanges the code at the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret and code.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers connect their individual Todoist accounts.

findings.title: data:read grants read-only access to tasks
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. It does not grant write permissions, so it is the least-privilege documented grant for listing active task titles.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing active task titles without creating, updating, completing or deleting tasks.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Refresh tokens for ongoing access
findings.detail: Newly created apps have refresh tokens enabled by default, and the token response includes expires_in and refresh_token. Access tokens are refreshed by exchanging the refresh token at the token endpoint.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer sessions that outlive the initial access token.

steps.title: Register the Todoist app and configure a redirect URL
steps.detail: In the Todoist App Management Console create an app, configure one HTTPS redirect URL, and record the Client ID and Client Secret. Use a confidential client with client_secret_post for the first test. This step is a developer preparation step; it does not execute consent.
steps.doneWhen: The app exists with a Client ID, Client Secret and a configured redirect URL.

steps.title: Redirect the test user to the Todoist consent screen and check the callback
steps.detail: Send the test user to the documented authorization URL with scope=data:read, response_type=code and a state value. After consent, check that the callback carries the matching state and a code. This step does not exchange the code.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect contains a code and the same state value that was sent.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
task:add Grants permission to add new tasks (the application cannot read or modify any existing data).
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: POST the code to the documented token endpoint with client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri as form fields. Expected success is HTTP 200 with access_token, token_type and, when refresh tokens are enabled, expires_in and refresh_token.
steps.doneWhen: The response is HTTP 200 and contains access_token.

evidence.quote: by sending a POST request to the following endpoint:
Name Description client_id The Client ID of the Todoist application that you registered.
code The code that was sent in the query string to the redirect URL in the previous step.

steps.title: List the first page of active tasks and read content titles
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with a limit and bearer token. Read each result's content field as the task title. Expected success is HTTP 200 with a results array and next_cursor. Boundary check: the call makes no changes, and the response should contain no write fields used.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with a results array; each item's content is read as a title.

evidence.quote: Response JSON paths for get /api/v1/tasks: $.results (array)
Response JSON paths for get /api/v1/tasks: $.results[].content (string)
curl "https://api.todoist.com/api/v1/tasks?limit=50" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

steps.title: Request the next page of active tasks using next_cursor
steps.detail: Repeat the same request with the same limit and the cursor value from the previous response. Continue until next_cursor is null, which is the documented end condition.
steps.doneWhen: next_cursor is null on the final page. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
